contributions.statement: If you expose a code-execution (CodeAct) action to cut steps and tokens, measure repeated-run consistency too: Python CodeAct lowered pass^k for every actor while structured atomic view/edit/search tools were the only setup that raised it.
contributions.evidence: §3.2 Table 2 (65 SWE-bench Live instances, 10 rollouts, 3 actors): Atomic improves pass^5/7/9 for all actors (small absolute gains, e.g. Sonnet +0.017-0.031); Python lowers pass^k for all (audit). Table 8 step reductions ~28-40%. No CIs; Python repos only.

contributions.statement: Leave scratchpad and hypothesis-tracking 'think' tools out of the agent's tool catalog; they produced mixed or negative changes and actors mostly restated existing reasoning in them.
contributions.evidence: §3.5 Table 2 deltas for Scratchpad/HypoTrack; Appendix C qualitative trajectory analysis. Scoped to lightweight scaffolds.

reason: A controlled, capability-matched tool-interface study whose consistency and scratchpad results are specific enough to shape which MCP/CLI tools the team exposes; magnitudes are small and Python-only.
